verdict.rationale: AI Gateway documents a detailed request log. The Logs page supports search, filtering, live follow, a per-request routing view and CSV/JSON export, and the gateway records spend, model usage and observability metrics. The docs never say that request/response payloads, latency, token counts or cost are attached to each logged request. missing for 10: request/response body inspection, per-request latency, per-request token counts, per-request cost, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can inspect logged requests and responses with latency, token counts, and cost attached

citations.quote: The Requests section displays summaries by project, API key, and a detailed log of all requests.
open the Logs page, where you can search by request ID, filter by model, provider, or status code, follow requests live, and open one request to see how it was routed.
The AI Gateway logs spend, model usage, and observability metrics related to your requests, which you can use to monitor and debug.
centralize credentials, log requests, control spend
